name: Oregon
headline_status: Recreational and medical cannabis are legal in Oregon for adults 21+.
summary: Oregon voters approved Measure 91 in November 2014, and adult possession and home growing became legal on July 1, 2015; early sales to adults began at medical dispensaries on October 1, 2015. Adults 21+ may carry up to 2 ounces of flower in public and grow four plants per household, and retail purchases carry a 17% state tax plus up to 3% local tax. The Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission regulates the market, which has operated under population-based license caps since HB 4121 in 2024, and a 2025 law (HB 3825) reinforced the state's ban on artificially derived cannabinoids such as delta-8 THC.

adult_use_since.value: July 1, 2015, under Measure 91, which voters approved in November 2014.

possession_limit.value: Up to 2 oz of flower in public (raised from 1 oz by SB 408 in 2021) and up to 8 oz of usable cannabis at home.

home_grow.value: Four plants per residence, no matter how many adults live there.

public_use.value: Smoking or using cannabis in public is not allowed; businesses with a liquor license, including patios and decks, count as public, and the Indoor Clean Air Act also applies.

retail_sales.value: Early sales to adults began October 1, 2015 at medical dispensaries; adults may buy up to 2 oz of flower per transaction since January 1, 2022. New licenses are capped by population under HB 4121 (2024).

taxes.value: 17% state retail tax on recreational cannabis, plus up to 3% local tax where cities or counties adopt it.

medical_program.value: Registered patients may possess up to 24 oz and grow up to six mature and 12 immature plants; the annual patient fee is $200, with reductions for veterans, SNAP/SSI recipients and Oregon Health Plan members.

hemp_thc.value: HB 3825 (2025) reinforces Oregon's prohibition on CBN, delta-8 THC and other artificially derived cannabinoids and calls for clearer testing and labeling standards.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Oregon has no THC per se limit; driving under the influence of intoxicants (DUII) includes impairment from marijuana.

tourists.value: Yes. Licensed retailers sell to customers 21+ with valid ID, up to 2 ounces of usable marijuana, 16 ounces of solid edibles, 72 fluid ounces of liquid products and 10 grams of extracts per day.

timeline.event: Voters approve Measure 67, creating the medical marijuana program
Voters approve Measure 91, legalizing adult-use cannabis
Adult possession and home cultivation become legal
Early adult-use sales begin at medical dispensaries
Per-transaction purchase limit for flower rises to 2 oz
HB 4121 replaces the license moratorium with population-based caps
HB 3825 signed, reinforcing the ban on artificially derived cannabinoids

faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older have been able to possess and grow cannabis since July 1, 2015, and licensed stores sell to adults.

faq.q: How much weed can you carry in Oregon?
faq.a: Up to 2 ounces of flower in public, and up to 8 ounces at home.

faq.q: Can you grow weed in Oregon?
faq.a: Yes. Adults may grow four plants per residence, regardless of how many people live there.

faq.q: What is the weed tax in Oregon?
faq.a: Recreational purchases carry a 17% state tax, and cities or counties can add up to 3% more.

faq.q: Is delta-8 THC legal in Oregon?
faq.a: No. Oregon bars artificially derived cannabinoids such as delta-8 THC, a ban reinforced by HB 3825 in 2025.
